Hi Anita — thanks for the quick reply and the topology diagram. High-level answers below; happy to go deeper on the call.

Short answers (Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private)
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, but shared runtime by default — not recommended for PHI unless using our Private offering.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, per-tenant scheduling, and stronger isolation guarantees (recommended path for MedLytics if you want predictable latency and cost).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full tenancy control and network isolation; higher ops onboarding but matches strict regulatory constraints.

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we provide for Dedicated
- Reserved GPU pools per customer and tenant-aware scheduling to avoid cross-tenant GPU batching when requested.
- Runtime limits and QoS: CUDA stream cgrouping + GPU clock limiting to enforce worst-case isolation contracts.
- KV cache scoping: per-tenant KV namespaces, no cross-tenant cache sharing.
- Predictability: conservative autoscale policies + preemptible instance safeguards; an escape hatch to route traffic to a pinned private allocation if we detect tail-latency anomalies.

SLO examples we can commit to for Dedicated (examples from similar PHI customers)
- p95 token latency: <= 180 ms (seq len 256)
- p99 token latency: <= 400 ms (seq len 256)
- Throughput SLA: baseline X tokens/sec per reserved GPU (we'll run a short benchmark against your payload to size accurately)

Artifacts we can provide this week
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted)
- Network diagram for our VPC peering options and a sample contract/PO template
- Updated tenant-separation-checklist.xlsx with explicit rows for the runtime controls above (attached).

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive (30 min): Wed 06/21 10:00-10:30am ET or Thu 06/22 2:00-2:30pm ET — which works best?
- I'll run a quick sizing benchmark if you can share a representative request (payload shape + token lengths).
- I'll include a ballpark cost-delta table (Dedicated vs Private) in the follow-up so procurement has a sense of run-rate impact.

If helpful, I'll also put together a short "incident runbook" excerpt that describes detection and remediation for noisy-neighbor events.
